questions: If you use public fast chargers part of the time, will the energy cost per km still be clearly below the hybrid's fuel cost?
What is your expectation of cheap charging based on: an advertised price, a friend's experience, or your own calculation?
If you cannot charge at home, would your workplace offer a charger and at what price per kWh?
Can you get written permission from your landlord or building manager to install a charger or use a socket at your parking spot?
What would insurance and yearly road tax cost for each car, based on quotes?
What does a battery health report show for the specific used EV you are considering?
Do your employer or the city offer a charging benefit, a commuting subsidy, or a purchase incentive?
What are similar five-year-old cars of each type selling for today, compared with their price new?
Can you have a garage inspect the EV and take a short return period before you commit?
On a cold winter morning with heating on and at highway speed, how many kilometres would this EV really drive on a full charge?

criteria: Total cost of ownership over 5 years at 60 km per day, including purchase, energy, maintenance, insurance, tax and resale value, is lowest
Charging is practical every working day with little effort, given the rented apartment
Little hassle: breakdowns, repairs, downtime and range anxiety are limited over the 5 years
Purchase price stays within the fixed budget
stated_facts: Goal is lowest total cost over 5 years for a 60 km daily commute, with no hassle
Used EV costs about the same as the new hybrid
Electricity per km is much cheaper than fuel locally

assumptions.text: Home or workplace charging will be available at a low per-km electricity price.
The used EV's battery will last the full 5 years with acceptable range and no costly replacement.
Maintenance savings on the EV outweigh the lack of a new-car warranty.
Energy and maintenance are the main cost differences; depreciation and insurance are similar.

uncertainties.text: Can the user charge cheaply and reliably, given the rented apartment: is there a landlord-approved wall charger or a parking spot with a socket, or a charger at work?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If cheap overnight or workplace charging is available, the EV is favored; if the user must rely on public fast chargers at higher prices, the cost advantage shrinks and the hybrid is favored.

uncertainties.text: What is the battery's state of health and warranty status for this specific used EV, and what is the cost of failure?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the battery health is good with remaining warranty, the EV is favored; if it is degraded or unwarranted, the replacement risk could cancel the savings and favor the hybrid.

uncertainties.text: What is the real winter and highway range of the used EV compared with the 60 km daily need plus any longer trips?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If range comfortably covers the commute with margin in cold weather, the EV is favored; if it is tight, hassle and charging frequency favor the hybrid.

uncertainties.text: What are expected resale values after 5 years for each car, given EV depreciation and battery concerns versus hybrid residual value?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If used EV resale holds up, it is favored; if EV values drop sharply, the hybrid's total cost may be lower.

uncertainties.text: How do insurance, road tax, and any incentives or local rules (low-emission zones, parking) differ between the two cars?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If the EV has tax or access benefits, it is favored; if insurance for a used EV is higher, the gap narrows toward the hybrid.

uncertainties.text: Does the user also need to take occasional long trips, and how well are the routes covered by fast charging?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If long trips are rare or well covered by chargers, the EV is favored; if frequent, the hybrid's convenience is favored.

uncertainties.text: Could the user move before 5 years or lose their parking arrangement, changing charging access?
uncertainties.if_resolved: If housing is stable, the EV plan holds; if a move is likely to a place without charging, the hybrid is favored.

chosen.question: If you use public fast chargers part of the time, will the energy cost per km still be clearly below the hybrid's fuel cost?
chosen.why: Checks the link between electricity being cheap and the savings you would actually see.
chosen.answer_path: Calculate cost per km using local public charging prices and the car's consumption, and compare with the hybrid's fuel use at current pump prices.

chosen.question: What is your expectation of cheap charging based on: an advertised price, a friend's experience, or your own calculation?
chosen.why: Charging prices vary a lot between home, work and public stations.
chosen.answer_path: Collect your actual local tariff for home and public charging and recalculate.

chosen.question: If you cannot charge at home, would your workplace offer a charger and at what price per kWh?
chosen.why: The savings assume cheap charging, which a rented apartment may not provide.
chosen.answer_path: Ask your employer's facilities team and check the pricing of public chargers on your commute.

chosen.question: Can you get written permission from your landlord or building manager to install a charger or use a socket at your parking spot?
chosen.why: Cheap overnight charging makes the used EV much stronger; without it the hybrid gains.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the landlord or property manager in writing, and ask neighbours who charge whether they have a shared arrangement.

chosen.question: What would insurance and yearly road tax cost for each car, based on quotes?
chosen.why: These costs are unknown and could close or widen the gap.
chosen.answer_path: Request quotes from two or three insurers for both cars, and check the tax rules for each on the transport authority's site.

chosen.question: What does a battery health report show for the specific used EV you are considering?
chosen.why: A healthy battery supports the EV; a worn one could erase the savings.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the seller for a state-of-health test or a dealer printout, and have an independent garage verify it.

chosen.question: Do your employer or the city offer a charging benefit, a commuting subsidy, or a purchase incentive?
chosen.why: Such support could lower the EV's cost or the charging problem.
chosen.answer_path: Ask your HR team and look at national and local incentive sites.

chosen.question: What are similar five-year-old cars of each type selling for today, compared with their price new?
chosen.why: Resale value changes which car costs less over five years.
chosen.answer_path: Search used-car listings for both models at the age and mileage yours would reach, and ask a dealer about expected values.

chosen.question: Can you have a garage inspect the EV and take a short return period before you commit?
chosen.why: Reduces the risk of a purchase that is hard to undo.
chosen.answer_path: Ask the seller about inspection and return terms, and book an independent pre-purchase check.

chosen.question: On a cold winter morning with heating on and at highway speed, how many kilometres would this EV really drive on a full charge?
chosen.why: Tests whether the range covers the 60 km daily commute with a buffer.
chosen.answer_path: Look up real-world winter range tests for the model, and ask current owners or the seller to demonstrate a cold-weather drive.

candidates.question: How much does a replacement battery cost for this model, and is there any warranty left for it?
candidates.why: The EV plan assumes no costly battery replacement over five years.
candidates.answer_path: Check the manufacturer's battery warranty terms by age and mileage, and ask a dealer for a replacement quote.

candidates.question: How much would you save on maintenance with the EV, and how does that compare with a hybrid under warranty?
candidates.why: Checks whether the warranty gap is covered by lower maintenance.
candidates.answer_path: Ask a garage for service-plan prices for both models and read the warranty terms of the new hybrid.

candidates.question: Are depreciation and insurance really similar for the two, or does one lose value much faster?
candidates.why: The comparison treats them as equal, which may not be right.
candidates.answer_path: Compare price history of similar cars in listings and compare insurance quotes.

candidates.question: On a cold winter morning with heating on and at highway speed, how many kilometres would this EV really drive on a full charge?
candidates.why: Tests whether the range covers the 60 km daily commute with a buffer.
candidates.answer_path: Look up real-world winter range tests for the model, and ask current owners or the seller to demonstrate a cold-weather drive.

candidates.question: If you use public fast chargers part of the time, will the energy cost per km still be clearly below the hybrid's fuel cost?
candidates.why: Checks the link between electricity being cheap and the savings you would actually see.
candidates.answer_path: Calculate cost per km using local public charging prices and the car's consumption, and compare with the hybrid's fuel use at current pump prices.

candidates.question: Do owners of used EVs of this age report fewer or more repair bills than owners of new hybrids?
candidates.why: Checks the cause-and-effect link between EV simplicity and low maintenance.
candidates.answer_path: Read owner forums and reliability surveys for the model, and ask an independent mechanic.

candidates.question: Does charging time on a trip add enough delay and effort to matter compared with filling up a hybrid?
candidates.why: Tests whether the no-hassle goal holds on longer journeys.
candidates.answer_path: Plan your most typical long trip with a route planner that includes charging stops and compare the total time.

candidates.question: At what daily distance or temperature would the used EV no longer cover your commute without charging at work or on the way?
candidates.why: Defines the conditions under which the EV stops working for you.
candidates.answer_path: Use the car's winter range figures and compare them with your 60 km commute plus detours, then calculate the margin.

candidates.question: How much battery degradation per year would the car need to show before range becomes a problem within five years?
candidates.why: Gives a limit on how much battery loss you can accept.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the seller for the current capacity and compare it with typical degradation rates for that model.

candidates.question: How many days per week could you cope with having to charge at a public station?
candidates.why: Shows how much charging inconvenience the EV choice can absorb.
candidates.answer_path: Map public chargers near home and work, check how busy they get in the evening, and try a week on them.

candidates.question: If your fuel price or electricity price changed by a large amount, at what point would the cheaper option switch?
candidates.why: Finds the energy price conditions that decide between the cars.
candidates.answer_path: Build a simple five-year cost model and test different energy price scenarios.

candidates.question: Is there a car-sharing, leasing or subscription option that would reduce the risk of ownership?
candidates.why: Adds other ways to get the car that the two options do not cover.
candidates.answer_path: Search local leasing and subscription providers and compare their five-year cost with buying.

candidates.question: Would a used hybrid or a new EV fit within your fixed budget and change the comparison?
candidates.why: The two options may not be the best ones within the budget.
candidates.answer_path: Check listings for a used hybrid and for the cheapest new EV, and compare their five-year costs.

candidates.question: Do your employer or the city offer a charging benefit, a commuting subsidy, or a purchase incentive?
candidates.why: Such support could lower the EV's cost or the charging problem.
candidates.answer_path: Ask your HR team and look at national and local incentive sites.

candidates.question: Could public transport or a mix of train and car handle part of the 60 km commute for less?
candidates.why: The goal is the lowest cost with no hassle, which cars might not satisfy.
candidates.answer_path: Compare the monthly pass price and journey time against the running costs of either car.

candidates.question: How likely is it that you will move or change jobs within five years, and what would that do to the commute?
candidates.why: A change would affect which car makes sense.
candidates.answer_path: Check your lease end date and your job's stability, and write down how likely each change is.

candidates.question: Can you have a garage inspect the EV and take a short return period before you commit?
candidates.why: Reduces the risk of a purchase that is hard to undo.
candidates.answer_path: Ask the seller about inspection and return terms, and book an independent pre-purchase check.

candidates.question: Is there a deadline, such as an expiring offer, incentive, or the end of your current car's life, that forces the decision?
candidates.why: Shows what waiting actually costs.
candidates.answer_path: Check the dates on any offers, your current car's condition and the timing of any incentive changes.

candidates.question: Which of the two would be easier to sell if you needed to get out of it after two years?
candidates.why: Shows which choice is easier to undo.
candidates.answer_path: Check how long similar used EVs and hybrids sit on listing sites and how much they lose in the first two years.

candidates.question: What is your expectation of cheap charging based on: an advertised price, a friend's experience, or your own calculation?
candidates.why: Charging prices vary a lot between home, work and public stations.
candidates.answer_path: Collect your actual local tariff for home and public charging and recalculate.

candidates.question: Where does your confidence in the used EV's battery come from: the seller, a report, or general reputation?
candidates.why: A seller's statement is weaker evidence than a test.
candidates.answer_path: Compare what the seller says with an independent battery test.

candidates.question: What is the basis for believing that energy and maintenance are the only differences that matter?
candidates.why: Other costs may be left out because they are harder to see.
candidates.answer_path: List every cost for five years for both cars and see which items you have only guessed.

candidates.question: How often do you take trips much longer than your commute, and are you recalling real trips or imagining them?
candidates.why: Occasional trips may be more or less frequent than assumed.
candidates.answer_path: Check your calendar, fuel receipts or navigation history for the last year.
